article_content: By Lizzie Edmonds. Published at 13:36 EST, 23 January 2014. Updated at 14:37 EST, 23 January 2014. These pictures show serial killer Joanna Dennehy and one of her alleged accomplices, Gary Stretch Richards, walking hand in hand through a service station while police were searching for them. In CCTV footage shown to jurors at Cambridge Crown Court, the 31-year-old killer and her 7ft 3in accomplice can be seen wandering through Strensham services off the M5, south of Worcester. In the footage, filmed at 8:43am on April 2 of last year, Richards is seen putting his arm around Dennehy. Dennehy, who appears to have a pair of handcuffs attached to her jeans, then waits for him outside the toilets. After about 10 minutes in the service station, they head outside before driving to Hereford in a Vauxhall Astra. Later that day, Dennehy randomly selected and repeatedly stabbed two strangers, Robin Bereza and John Rogers, as they walked their dogs in Hereford. Both men survived. By then, Dennehy and Richards were wanted by police following the discovery of the body of Kevin Lee near Peterborough the previous day. A farmer discovered the bodies of two other victims, Lukasz Slaboszewski and John Chapman, in a ditch on April 3. The court heard that Dennehy drove to Hereford soon after this footage and stabbed two random strangers. Richards is accused of driving 140 miles from Cambridgeshire to Hereford, passing through Suffolk, Norfolk, and Leicestershire, while Dennehy sought victims. Dennehy, of Orton Goldhay, Peterborough, admitted murdering Mr Slaboszewski, 31, Mr Chapman, 56, and Mr Lee, 48. She also admitted the attempted murders of Mr Bereza and Mr Rogers, and preventing the lawful burial of all three murder victims. Earlier in the week, pictures of Dennehy posing with a knife while she was wanted by police were shown to the jury. In another photo, she is seen with her top lifted, exposing her underwear. Richards is also pictured posing in a photograph. Richards, 47, of Riseholme, Orton Goldhay, Peterborough, denied three counts of preventing the lawful burial of the three men and two counts of attempted murder. Layton, 36, of Bifield, Orton Goldhay, denied perverting the course of justice and two counts of preventing the lawful burial of Mr Chapman and Mr Lee. A third man, Robert Moore, 55, of Belvoir Way, Peterborough, admitted assisting an offender and is awaiting sentencing. The trial of Richards and Layton continues, with the court scheduled to hear their defense.

article_content: By Matt Blake. Published: 06:10 EST, 3 May 2012. Updated: 10:44 EST, 3 May 2012. A former specialist police officer who worked for Scotland Yard’s division in charge of protecting the Royal Family was arrested today by detectives investigating corrupt payments to public officials. Police from Operation Elveden, which operates alongside the force’s Weeting investigation into phone hacking, arrived at the 57-year-old man’s home in Surrey early this morning. The retired officer served in the Metropolitan Police’s Specialist Operations command, which handles various security tasks from providing armed protection for MPs and the Royal Family to gathering counter-terrorism intelligence. During the dawn raid, officers took him in for questioning on suspicion of misconduct in a public office. This is the 27th arrest by detectives under Operation Elveden. A police statement said: ‘The 57-year-old man was arrested at his home address. He previously served in the MPS Specialist Operations command, based in central London, and retired several years ago. He is currently being questioned at a south-west London police station, and his home address is being searched.’ The force added that the arrest ‘is not about seeking journalists to reveal confidential sources in relation to information that has been obtained legitimately.’ The arrest comes two weeks after The Sun’s royal editor, Duncan Larcombe, was arrested along with a 42-year-old former member of the Armed Forces and a 38-year-old woman as part of the same inquiry. Last month, The Sun’s defence editor Virginia Wheeler, 32, was held on suspicion of illegal payments to police. The Sun’s deputy editor Geoff Webster, picture editor John Edwards, chief reporter John Kay, chief foreign correspondent Nick Parker, and news editor John Sturgis were arrested in February. In January, former managing editor Graham Dudman, executive editor Fergus Shanahan, crime editor Mike Sullivan, and head of news Chris Pharo were also detained and later bailed. These arrests followed an internal investigation by News International, now reorganized as News UK, after the phone-hacking scandal that led to the closure of the News of the World in July 2011. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed last month that it has received the first set of files from police regarding these inquiries.

article_content: Cape Town, South Africa (CNN) -- Off track, Tasneem Howa is a rather introverted young woman who works as a photographer in Cape Town. On track, however, she puts on black tights and slips into roller skates to transform into 'TazMEANian Devil,' a fierce diva on wheels. 'When I put on skates, it's a rush,' she says. 'You feel free, the wind on your face; it's awesome.' 'TazMEANian Devil' is a proud member of the Rev'ettes, one of three roller derby teams in the women-only Cape Town Rollergirls league. Many, like her, joined the sport after watching the 2009 film 'Whip It,' starring and directed by Drew Barrymore. 'I thought it was girls bashing into each other, but it's calmer than that,' she notes. Fast-paced and full-contact, roller derby requires endurance, teamwork, and frequent crashes. Body checks are common as players circle a flat oval track to prevent opponents from scoring points. 'You can be dainty but need to be slightly aggressive,' says Ming-Cheau Lin, also known as 'Wolverming,' who plays for the Storm Riders. One major tradition is adopting a derby name that reflects an alter ego. 'It may seem silly, but historically people wanted to remain anonymous,' says Shawn Graaff, who founded Cape Town Rollergirls in 2010. 'They didn't want to compromise their professional careers by being involved in an aggressive spectacle.' Roller derby emerged as a competitive U.S. sport in the 1930s, eventually becoming more theatrical, akin to WWE. Its popularity declined in the 1980s, but an all-women's league in Texas reinvented it in the early 2000s, emphasizing athleticism. Drew Barrymore's 'Whip It' brought renewed attention worldwide, including South Africa. The Cape Town Rollergirls league is made up of three teams: the Rev'ettes, the Storm Riders, and the Iron Meisies, featuring everyone from working mothers to expats. Men mainly coach or referee. Graaff says the sport challenges stereotypes, showing women can be both tough and feminine. 'We celebrate our femininity while highlighting our strength,' she says. For mothers like Elisabeth Hansen Dreyer, or 'Betty Blizzard,' roller derby is liberating. 'It will save your sanity,' says the Storm Riders blocker. 'After a day with screaming kids, you get to go bump girls. It's awesome!' Now, with an officiating director from the international governing body set to visit, the league hopes for further growth—and more bruises.

article_content: headline: New Mexico Woman Allegedly Smuggles Handgun Into Jail Through Private Parts Authorities in Albuquerque say 34-year-old Josephine McAllister was arrested on December 16 on multiple charges, including possession of stolen credit cards, larceny, receiving stolen property, and resisting or obstructing an officer. Shortly after McAllister was booked into the Bernalillo County Metropolitan Detention Center, another inmate discovered a handgun in the women’s restroom while disposing of trash. McAllister allegedly smuggled the firearm inside her body, although she initially claimed it was hidden in her waistband. Officers suspect the gun was concealed in her genitals. She said she did not inform the police about the weapon to avoid additional charges. Officer Simon Drobik told local station KOAT that four officers searched McAllister thoroughly but could not conduct a body cavity search due to departmental policies. Authorities stated that once suspects arrive at the jail, they undergo a body scanner and a pat-down. However, McAllister apparently asked to use the restroom before a thorough search could be conducted. Since this incident, jail officials have introduced new security protocols, including wanding detainees upon arrival, posting staff near restrooms, and checking facilities before and after use. McAllister now faces an additional charge of bringing contraband into a place of imprisonment. Records indicate she has been arrested numerous times since 2003 on charges ranging from shoplifting to drug possession, burglary, and probation violations. McAllister, a mother of four, has drawn attention due to her repeated run-ins with the law. Her grown daughter commented on social media that the searches conducted by officers are insufficient, insisting McAllister would never hurt anyone.

Her relatives ended up with only a fraction of the inheritance.' 'Paragraph 2: The court heard that the Edinburgh-based firm, led by director Alexander Pilley, charged excessive commissions and expenses amounting to over £132,000. They insisted that if the family did not sign the contract, they would obtain nothing at all.' 'Paragraph 4: Judge Richard Parkes described the fraud as calculated and cynical, ordering the firm to pay £200,000 in compensation and imposing a £25,000 fine. Yet, the victims have received no payment, and the company's assets appear nonexistent.'

article_content: By Associated Press Reporter. PUBLISHED: 00:37 EST, 20 November 2013 | UPDATED: 00:37 EST, 20 November 2013. A sharply divided Supreme Court on Tuesday allowed Texas to continue enforcing abortion restrictions that opponents say have led more than a third of the state’s clinics to stop providing abortions. The justices voted 5-4 to keep in effect a provision requiring doctors who perform abortions to have admitting privileges at a nearby hospital. Planned Parenthood and several Texas abortion clinics sought to have the provision overturned, but the court’s conservative majority refused. The four liberal justices dissented. The case remains on appeal to the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in New Orleans, which is set to hear arguments in January. Justice Stephen Breyer, writing for the liberal justices, said the issue will likely return to the Supreme Court after the appeals court issues its final ruling. Texas’s admitting privileges requirement was approved in July. Days before it was to take effect, a federal judge blocked it, calling it likely unconstitutional for placing a substantial obstacle before women seeking abortions. However, a three-judge appellate panel quickly overruled that decision. The appeals court argued that the law aligns with Supreme Court rulings permitting abortion restrictions that do not impose an undue burden. Judge Priscilla Owen noted that while the restriction might make women travel farther, it does not end the procedure. Justice Antonin Scalia, supporting Tuesday’s order, said the clinics did not meet the heavy burden needed to overturn the appeals court’s ruling. Planned Parenthood and Texas abortion clinics said the provision forced over one-third of clinics to stop providing abortions or drastically reduce patient numbers. Justice Breyer observed that if the law is ultimately found invalid, the harm to women unable to obtain abortions during its enforcement would be permanent. Republican Texas Gov. Rick Perry praised the action, stating it protects women from unsafe conditions. Cecile Richards, president of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, promised continued legal efforts, calling for stronger federal protections to ensure women’s rights do not depend on their ZIP code. Similar admitting privilege laws exist in Tennessee and Utah and are under court injunctions in other states. In Texas, some clinics have been unable to secure hospital privileges. As a result, only around 20 facilities remain open in a state of 26 million people, mainly in metropolitan areas. The state sees about 80,000 abortions each year.

Manni murtii sun sagalee 5-4’n seera doktooronni ulfa baasuuf odiitii gaggeessan waraqaa hayyama hospitaalota naannoo sana jiraniin qabachuu qaban itti fufsiisuun ni danda’ama jedhe. Planned Parenthood fi kilinikoonni ulfa kan Texas hedduun seera kana haquuf mana murtii seenuun yaalan, garuu miseensonni mana murtii mooraa kanneen seera uggura ulfa deggaran didanii jiru. Miseensonni mana murtii afran, kan mooraa librelaa, morman. Dhimmichi ammas mana murtii olaanaa 5ffaa U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals kan New Orleans jiru keessatti mirga falmii argata, kanaaf jedhamuun ji’a Amajjii keessatti dhaggeeffatamuu eegama. Justice Stephen Breyer, kan miseensonni librelaa woliin barreesse, murtiin dhumaa mana murtii deebi’ee gaafa kennamu, dhimmichi gara Mana Murtii Waliigalaatti deebi’a jedhe. Seerri Texas ‘admitting privileges’ jedhamu kun muddee darbe ragga’e. Guyyoota muraasa dura, mana murtii sadarkaa duraa tokkoon akka seerri sun ugguramu taasifame, sababiin isaas seerri kun dubartoota ulfa baasuuf deeman daandii cufuu mala jedhame. Garuu, koreen manneen murtii sadii ol’aantuun murtii uggura kana diige. Manneen murtii ol’aantoon akka jedhanitti, seerri kun murtilee Mana Murtii Waliigalaa Dachee Ameerikaatiin walsimu; seerri uggura ulfa daangeessu humnaan hin dhorku yoo hatayyu malee, humna sodaa nama baasu hin ta’u. Judge Priscilla Owen, seerichi dubartoota fageenya dheeraa imaluuf dirqisiisus garuu carraan ulfa baasuu hin dhabamu jetti. Justice Antonin Scalia, kan murtii Kibxata deeggare, kilinikoonni seera kana gufachiisuu barbaadan ragaa cimaan hin dhiyeessine jedhe. Planned Parenthood fi kilinikoonni ulfa kan Texas, seerri kun sadarkaa ulfa baasuu kennan keessaa sadii ol kan cufsiise yookin dandeetti isaanii hir’ise jechuu dhaan ibsan. Justice Breyer hubachiisuudhaan seerri kun yoo dhumarratti seeraan ala ta’e jedhame, dubartoota yeroo seerri kun hojiirra turetti ulfa baasuu hin dandeenyeef rakkoon isaanii bara baraan tura jedhe. Gov. Rick Perry, kan paartii Ripabilikaanii mootummaa Texas, murtii kana ni dinqisiifate, akka dubartoota rakkoo teeknikaa kaasu ni eegu jadhe. Cecile Richards, prezidaantii Planned Parenthood Federation of America, falmii seeraa itti fufuuf waadaa seene; seerri kun mirga dubartoonni ulfa baasuu dhaan of kabachiisan waggoota 40f ture daangessa jedhe. Fedhii dubartootaa akka bakkaan hin galleef kuni rakkoo guddaadha, kanaaf naannoon kee mirga kee murteessuu hin qabu jedhe. Lawwan admitting privileges kan fakkaatan Tennessee fi Utah keessatti hojiirra jiru, akkasumas Alabama, Kansas, Mississippi, North Dakota fi Wisconsin keessatti ammoo hin hojiirra oolle sababin manneen murtii uggura kaa’aniin. Texas keessatti, kilinikoota ulfa 12 keessaa heddun hospitaala irraa waraqaa hayyamaa argachuuf yaalan, garuu ammatti hin arganne. Kanaaf, kilinikoonni sun ulfa baasuu hin kennine. Hanga yoonaatti kilinikoota 20’f gad hin caalle tu hojiirra jira, yoo xiqqaate magaalaa guddittan keessatti. Jumlaan uummanni Texas miliyoona 26 ta’uun himame. Sababa kanaan, waggaatti ulfa 80,000 ni baasu.
